competition: Kazakhstan Republican Mathematical Olympiad (Final Round, Grade 11)

problems.problem: Let $(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2014})$ be a permutation of $1,2,\ldots,2014$. What is the greatest possible number of perfect squares among $$a_1^2+a_2,\ a_2^2+a_3,\ \ldots,\ a_{2013}^2+a_{2014},\ a_{2014}^2+a_1?$$
Do there exist positive integers $a,b$ such that $a^n+n^b$ and $b^n+n^a$ are relatively prime for every positive integer $n$?

A triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$. Its incircle touches side $BC$ at $N$. A circle $\omega$ is inscribed in the circular segment of $\Gamma$ bounded by chord $BC$ and arc $BAC$, and passes through $N$. Let $O$ be the centre of $\omega$ and $J$ the centre of the excircle of $ABC$ touching side $BC$. Prove that lines $AO$ and $JN$ are parallel.

In a scalene triangle $ABC$, the incircle touches sides $AB$ and $BC$ at $C_1$ and $A_1$, respectively. The excircle touching side $AC$ touches the lines $AB$ and $BC$ at $C_2$ and $A_2$, respectively. Let $N$ be the point where the bisector of $\angle ABC$ meets side $AC$. Lines $A_1C_1$ and $A_2C_2$ meet line $AC$ at $K_1$ and $K_2$, respectively. For $i=1,2$, the circumcircle of $BK_iN$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $P_i\ne B$. Prove that $AP_1=CP_2$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q$ such that $$f(x,y)+f(y,z)+f(z,x)=f(0,x+y+z)$$ for all rational numbers $x,y,z$.
Prove that, for every positive integer $n$, the interval $$[n-4\sqrt n,\ n+4\sqrt n]$$ contains a number of the form $x^3+y^3$, where $x,y$ are nonnegative integers.
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Prove that, for every positive integer $m$, there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which the number of positive divisors of $na^n+1$ is divisible by $m$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Points $K$ and $M$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $AD$, respectively. Segments $AK$ and $BM$ meet at $N$, and segments $KD$ and $CM$ meet at $L$. Suppose quadrilateral $KLMN$ is cyclic. The circumcircles of $BNK$ and $AMN$ meet again at $Q\ne N$, and the circumcircles of $KLC$ and $DML$ meet again at $P\ne L$. Prove that quadrilaterals $KLMN$ and $KPMQ$ have equal areas.

There are $2015$ points in the plane, with no three collinear and no four concyclic. Consider the circles passing through three of these points and dividing the remaining points into two equal groups: $1006$ inside and $1006$ outside the circle. Prove that at least three such circles pass through the same two points of the given set.

In a triangle $ABC$, let $N$ be the point where the bisector of $\angle ACB$ meets $AB$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$, and let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$. Line $CN$ meets $\omega$ again at $D\ne C$. Points $K$ and $L$ lie on segments $AD$ and $BD$, respectively, with $\angle ACK=\angle BCL$. The circumcircles of $ACK$ and $BCL$ meet again at $P\ne C$, and lines $DM$ and $KL$ meet at $Q$. Prove that $M,N,P,Q$ are concyclic.
Find all pairs $(n,k)$ of positive integers for which $$(n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+k)-k$$ is a perfect square.

The sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ is defined by $a_1=2015$, $a_2=2^{2015}$, and $$a_{n+2}=a_n+\left\lceil\frac{a_{n+1}}n\right\rceil$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that there are positive integers $M,c$ such that, for every $n\ge M$, the number $na_{a_n}+c$ is a perfect power. Here $\lceil x\rceil$ is the least integer not less than $x$, and a perfect power is a number of the form $m^k$ with integers $m>1$ and $k>1$.
Prove that all positive divisors of any given positive integer can be arranged around a circle so that, for every two neighbouring numbers, one divides the other.

Find all rational numbers $a$ for which there are infinitely many positive rational numbers $q$ such that the equation $$\lfloor x^a\rfloor\{x^a\}=q$$ has no rational solution $x$. Here $\lfloor t\rfloor$ and $\{t\}=t-\lfloor t\rfloor$ denote the integer part and fractional part of $t$, respectively.

Two circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ intersect at $X$ and $Y$, lie inside a circle $\Omega$, and are tangent to $\Omega$ at $A$ and $B$, respectively. Line $AB$ meets $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ again at $A_1$ and $B_1$, respectively. The incircle of the curvilinear triangle $A_1B_1X$, bounded by segment $A_1B_1$ and arcs of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ meeting at $X$, touches side $A_1B_1$ at $Z$. Prove that $\angle AXZ=\angle BXZ$.

In an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $CA=CB$, let $H$ be the midpoint of base $AB$ and $M$ the midpoint of $BH$. Let $HK$ be the altitude of triangle $ACH$, and let lines $CM$ and $BK$ meet at $L$. The line through $B$ perpendicular to $BC$ meets line $LH$ at $N$. Prove that $\angle ACB=2\angle BCN$.

There are $101$ blue points and $101$ red points in the plane, with no three of the $202$ points collinear. The sum of all pairwise distances between red points is $1$, the sum of all pairwise distances between blue points is $1$, and the sum of the distances between points of different colours is $400$. Prove that a straight line can separate all red points from all blue points.

An infinite strictly increasing sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ of positive real numbers satisfies $$a_{n+2}=(a_{n+1}-a_n)^{\sqrt n}+n^{-\sqrt n}$$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that, for every $C>0$, there is a positive integer $m(C)$ such that $a_{m(C)}>C$.

Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with circumcircle $\omega$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $C$ meets line $AB$ at $D$. The bisector of $\angle CDB$ meets segments $AC$ and $BC$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively. A point $M$ on side $AB$ satisfies $AK/BL=AM/BM$. The perpendiculars from $M$ to lines $KL$ and $DC$ meet lines $AC$ and $DC$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Prove that $\angle CQP=\tfrac12\angle ACB$.
Let $x,y,z\ge\tfrac12$ be real numbers with $x^2+y^2+z^2=1$. Prove that $$\left(\frac1x+\frac1y-\frac1z\right)\left(\frac1x-\frac1y+\frac1z\right)\ge2.$$

An infinite strictly increasing sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ of positive integers satisfies $a_{a_n}\le a_n+a_{n+3}$ for every $n\ge1$. Prove that there are infinitely many triples of positive integers $(k,l,m)$ with $k<l<m$ and $a_k+a_m=2a_l$.

An acute triangle $ABC$ with $AC>BC$ is inscribed in a circle with centre $O$, and $CD$ is a diameter of this circle. Point $K$ lies on ray $DA$ beyond $A$, and point $L$ lies on segment $BD$ with $DL>LB$, such that $\angle OKD=\angle BAC$ and $\angle OLD=\angle ABC$. Prove that line $KL$ passes through the midpoint of $AB$.

Consider all $100$-tuples $(x_1,\ldots,x_{100})$ of positive integers with $1\le x_i\le2017$ for every $i$. Say that $(y_1,\ldots,y_{100})$ is greater than $(z_1,\ldots,z_{100})$ if $y_i>z_i$ for every $i$. What is the largest number of distinct tuples that can be written on a board so that no tuple is greater than another?
Prove that there are infinitely many composite positive integers $n$ for which $n$ divides $2^{(n-1)/2}+1$.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezoid with bases $AD$ and $BC$, and let $O$ be the midpoint of $AD$. The circle with centre $O$ and radius $BO$ is tangent to line $AB$. Segment $AC$ meets this circle at $K\ne C$. Let $M$ be the point such that $ABCM$ is a parallelogram. The circumcircle of $CMD$ meets segment $AC$ again at $L\ne C$. Prove that $AK=CL$.

Let $m\ge2$ be an integer. A sequence $(b_0,b_1,\ldots,b_m)$ of positive integers is called concave if $b_k+b_{k-2}\le2b_{k-1}$ for every $2\le k\le m$. Prove that there are at most $2^m$ concave sequences with $b_0=1$ and $b_1=2$.
Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfying $$f(mf(n))=f(m)f(m+n)+n$$ for all positive integers $m,n$? Here $\mathbb N$ denotes the positive integers.
Prove that, for all real numbers $a,b,c,d\in(0,1)$, $$(ab-cd)(ac+bd)(ad-bc)+\min\{a,b,c,d\}<1.$$
Let $S=\{xy(x+y):x,y\text{ are positive integers}\}$. Suppose $a,n$ are positive integers such that $a+2^k\in S$ for every $k=1,2,\ldots,n$. Find the greatest possible value of $n$.

A point $M$ inside a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ satisfies $\angle AMB=\angle ADM+\angle BCM$ and $\angle AMD=\angle ABM+\angle DCM$. Prove that $$AM\cdot CM+BM\cdot DM\ge\sqrt{AB\cdot BC\cdot CD\cdot DA}.$$
Prove that, for all positive real numbers $a,b,c$, $$\sqrt[3]{\frac ab}+\sqrt[5]{\frac bc}+\sqrt[7]{\frac ca}>\frac52.$$

A finite set $\Phi$ of points in the plane has distance at least $\sqrt2$ between any two of its points. All points of $\Phi$ can be covered by an equilateral triangle of side length $3$. What is the greatest possible number of points in $\Phi$?
Let $p$ be a prime of the form $4k+1$, and write $$\sum_{a=2}^{p-2}\frac1{a^{(p-1)/2}+a^{(p+1)/2}}=\frac mn$$ in lowest terms. Prove that $p$ divides $m+n$.
Find all positive integers $n,k,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ such that $$(na_1+1)(na_2+1)\cdots(na_k+1)\mid n^{k+1}+1.$$

Let $n,m$ be positive integers. Is it always possible to mark three or four lattice points of an $n\times m$ rectangle on the unit square grid so that each line containing a side of the rectangle contains at least one marked point, and a non-self-intersecting polygon with the marked points as vertices has area $$\frac12\min\left\{\gcd(n,m),\frac{n+m}{\gcd(n,m)}\right\}?$$

A tangent line $\ell$ to the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$ meets lines $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$ at $C^{\prime}$, $A^{\prime}$, and $B^{\prime}$, respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocentre of $ABC$. Points $A_1,B_1,C_1$, each different from $H$, lie on lines $A^{\prime}H$, $B^{\prime}H$, $C^{\prime}H$, respectively, and satisfy $AH=AA_1$, $BH=BB_1$, and $CH=CC_1$. Prove that the circumcircles of $ABC$ and $A_1B_1C_1$ are tangent.
Find all pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers such that $$n^4\mid 2m^5-1,\qquad m^4\mid 2n^5+1.$$
Find all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $$f(x)f(y)=f\left(\frac{xy}{xf(x)+y}\right)$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

Let $CM$ be a median of a triangle $ABC$. A point $N$ on segment $CM$ satisfies $MN\cdot MC=AB^2/4$. Lines $AN$ and $BN$ meet the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $R$ be the point of segment $PQ$ nearest to $Q$ for which $\angle NRC=\angle BNC$, and let $S$ be the point of segment $PQ$ nearest to $P$ for which $\angle NSC=\angle ANC$. Prove that $RN=SN$.

Alice and Bob play on a strip of cells infinite in both directions, labelled by consecutive integers $\ldots,-2,-1,0,1,2,\ldots$. On her turn Alice places a cross in one empty cell, and on his turn Bob places zeros in $2020$ empty cells. They alternate, with Alice moving first. Alice wins if she obtains four cells marked with crosses whose labels form an arithmetic progression. Can Alice guarantee a win regardless of how Bob plays?

A shelf contains $100$ volumes of an encyclopedia, numbered $1,2,\ldots,100$, in an arbitrary order. In one operation any three volumes can be taken and rearranged in any order in their three positions. Find the least $m$ such that every initial arrangement can be put in order in at most $m$ operations. In order means that volume $i$ occupies position $i$ for every $i$.

Prove that there are infinitely many pairs $(a,b)$ of distinct positive integers such that, for every positive integer $n$, $$\left\lfloor\sqrt{a^2n}+\sqrt{b^2n+1}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\sqrt{(a+b)^2n+3}\right\rfloor.$$ Here $\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $x$.
A point $M$ inside a triangle $ABC$ satisfies $$\angle MCA=\max\{\angle MAB,\angle MBC,\angle MCA\}.$$ Prove that $\sin\angle MAB+\sin\angle MBC\le1$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcircle $\Gamma$ and altitudes $AD$, $BE$, and $CF$. Line $AD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $P$, and lines $PF$ and $PE$ meet $\Gamma$ again at $R$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the circumcentres of $BFR$ and $CEQ$, respectively. Prove that line $O_1O_2$ passes through the midpoint of $EF$.
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Prove that every integer solution $(x,y)$ of $$x(y^2-2x^2)+x+y+a=0$$ satisfies $|x|\le a+\sqrt{2a^2+2}$.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with real coefficients and $m$ a positive integer. Suppose that, for every positive integer $n$, there is an integer $l$ such that $P(l)=n^m$. Prove that $P(x)=(ax+b)^k$ for some real numbers $a,b$ and positive integer $k$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ the altitudes $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ are drawn. The points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the segments $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that the line $PQ$ is parallel to $BC$. The circles constructed on $BQ$ and $CP$ as diameters meet at the points $R$ and $T$ ($R$ is closer to $A$ than $T$). Let $CM$ and $BN$ be altitudes of triangle $BCR$. Prove that the lines $FM$, $NE$ and $AD$ pass through one point.

For a positive integer $A$, define $Z(A)$ as the number $A$ written in reverse order (for example, $Z(521) = 125$). A number $A$ is called good if its decimal representation contains no zeros, its first digit is not equal to its last digit, and $(Z(A))^2 = Z(A^2)$. Find all good numbers greater than $10^6$.

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$. Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ such that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$
$$f(f(x) + y) - f(x) = \left(\frac{f(y)}{y} - 1\right) \cdot x + f^{(m)}(y).$$
Here $f^{(m)}(y) = f(f(\dots f(y) \dots))$ ($m$ times).
A polynomial $P(x)$ of degree $699$ with positive integer coefficients is given, with $P(1) \le 2022$. Prove that there are several consecutive coefficients whose sum is equal to $22$, $55$ or $77$.

A cyclic convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given, with $O$ the intersection point of its diagonals. $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of the sides $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. On the arc $AB$ of the circumcircle of $ABCD$ not containing the points $C$ and $D$, a point $S$ is marked such that $\angle SMA = \angle SNB$. Let $T$ be the intersection point of the diagonals of the convex quadrilateral formed by the lines $SM$, $SN$, $AB$ and $CD$. Prove that the points $S$, $O$, $T$ lie on one line.

An infinite sequence of positive integers $\{a_n\}$ satisfies $a_{n+2} = a_na_{n+1} + 1$ for every $n \ge 1$. Prove that for every index $i$ there exists an index $j > i$ such that $a_j^j$ is divisible by $a_i^i$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with obtuse angle $C$ and $AC>BC$, and let $O$ be the centre of its circumcircle $\omega$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $C$ meets $AB$ at $D$. Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of $AOB$. Lines $OD$ and $AC$ meet $\Omega$ again at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Put $T=OF\cap CE$ and $K=OD\cap BC$. Prove that $OTBK$ is cyclic.

Let $n>100$ be an integer. The numbers $1,2,\ldots,4n$ are partitioned into $n$ groups of four. Prove that there are at least $(n-6)^2/2$ quadruples $(a,b,c,d)$ whose entries belong to four different groups and satisfy $$a<b<c<d,\qquad c-b\le |ad-bc|\le d-a.$$

Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers such that $$\max\left\{\frac{a(b+c)}{a^2+bc},\frac{b(c+a)}{b^2+ca},\frac{c(a+b)}{c^2+ab}\right\}\le\frac52.$$ Prove that $$\frac{a(b+c)}{a^2+bc}+\frac{b(c+a)}{b^2+ca}+\frac{c(a+b)}{c^2+ab}\le3.$$

In the plane there are $2000$ points, no three collinear, of which $1000$ are black and $1000$ are red. There are $100$ red points forming a convex $100$-gon with all the other $1900$ points strictly inside it. Prove that some segments joining points of the same colour can be drawn so that no segment joining red points intersects a segment joining black points, and the segments of each colour form a connected graph on all $1000$ points of that colour.

Let $a,b,m,k$ be positive integers with $k\ge2$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $$\gcd\left(\varphi_m(n),\left\lfloor\sqrt[k]{an+b}\right\rfloor\right)=1,$$ where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\varphi_m$ is its $m$-fold iterate.
Two rhombuses, each with side length $1.061$ and acute angle $60^\circ$, have all their vertices strictly inside an equilateral triangle of side length $3$. Prove that the two rhombuses intersect.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with altitude $AD$ and orthocentre $H$. A circle $\Omega$ passes through $A$ and $B$ and is tangent to line $AC$. Let $BE$ be a diameter of $\Omega$. Lines $BH$ and $AH$ meet $\Omega$ again at $K$ and $L$, respectively. Lines $EK$ and $AB$ meet at $T$. Prove that $\angle BDK=\angle BLT$.
Let $p\ge3$ be a prime and $d\ge1$ an integer. Prove that there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $\gcd(n,d)=1$ such that $$P=\prod_{1\le i<j<p}\left(i^{n+j}-j^{n+i}\right)$$ is not divisible by $p^n$.
Find all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $$f\left(x+\frac{f(xy)}x\right)=f(xy)f\left(y+\frac1y\right)$$ for all positive real numbers $x,y$.

Players $A$ and $B$ play a game on the coordinate plane. Player $A$ hides a nut at a point with integer coordinates, and player $B$ tries to find it. On each move, $B$ chooses three distinct points with integer coordinates, and $A$ tells $B$ whether these three points and the point containing the nut lie on one circle. Can $B$ be guaranteed to find the nut in finitely many moves?

Let $m\ge3$ be an integer, and let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers satisfying $$a_{n+2}=2\sqrt[m]{a_{n+1}^{m-1}+a_n^{m-1}}-a_{n+1}$$ for every $n\ge1$. Prove that $a_1<2^m$.

The incircle $\omega$ of a triangle $ABC$ with $AB\ne AC$ has centre $I$ and touches $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $D$, $E$, and $F$, respectively. The circumcircles of $ABC$ and $AEF$ meet again at $K$. Put $X=EF\cap AK$, $Y=EF\cap BC$, and $Z=AK\cap BC$. The tangents to $\omega$ from $Y$ and $Z$, other than line $BC$, touch $\omega$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Put $R=AP\cap KQ$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $YZ$. Prove that $IR\perp XM$.
Find all quadruples $(a,b,c,d)$ of positive integers such that $$2^a+3^b=5^c d,\qquad 2^b+3^a=5^d c.$$
Find all strictly increasing functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfying $$f(mf(n))+f(n)=f(nf(m))+f(m)$$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Here $\mathbb N$ denotes the positive integers.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$, incenter $I$, $A$-excenter $I_A$, altitude $AD$, and circumcircle $\Omega$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ of $\Omega$, and let $AL$ be a diameter of $\Omega$. Put $P=IL\cap I_AD$ and $Q=ID\cap I_AL$. A point $S$ satisfies $SA=SM$ and $SP=SL$. Prove that lines $AP$, $MQ$, and $I_AS$ are concurrent.

Let $x,y$ be positive real numbers and $n$ a positive integer such that $$\left\lfloor\frac{x^{n+1}}{y^n}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac xy\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{y^{n+1}}{x^n}\right\rfloor.$$ Prove that $$-\frac1{2n+1}<x-y<\frac2{2n-1}.$$ Here $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $t$.

Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle, $M$ the midpoint of $AB$, $I$ its incenter, and $J$ the midpoint of the arc $AB$ of its circumcircle not containing $C$. Tangents $IP$ and $IQ$ are drawn to the circle with centre $J$ and radius $JM$, with $A$ and $P$ on the same side of line $CI$. The circumcircles of $APJ$ and $BQJ$ meet again at $R$. Lines $IP$ and $IQ$ meet line $AB$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. The internal angle bisectors from $M$ in triangles $XMJ$ and $YMJ$ meet $XJ$ and $YJ$ at $X_1$ and $Y_1$, respectively. Prove that $X_1$, $Y_1$, and $R$ are collinear.

Let $n,k$ be positive integers with $k+1<2n$. Let $A$ be the set of sequences $(a_1,\ldots,a_{2n})$ such that $a_i\in\{1,-1\}$, $a_1+\cdots+a_{2n}=0$, and $a_1+\cdots+a_i\ge0$ for every $i=1,\ldots,2n$. Let $B=\{a\in A:a_k=1\}$ and $C=\{a\in A:a_{k+1}=1\}$. Prove that $$|B|\,|C|\ge |A|\,|B\cap C|,$$ where $|X|$ denotes the cardinality of $X$.

Does there exist an infinite set $S$ of positive integers such that (i) $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_{100})=1$ for every $100$ pairwise distinct elements $a_1,\ldots,a_{100}$ of $S$; and (ii) for every $x\in S$ there is $y\in S$ such that $x+y+2026$ divides $x^2$?

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle BAC=45^\circ$ and $\angle ABC>90^\circ$. The perpendicular from $A$ to line $BC$ meets the circumcircle of $ACD$ again at $E$. Line $EB$ meets diagonal $AC$ at $F$, and $EF=2AF$. Line $DF$ meets the circumcircle of $ACD$ again at $M$, and lines $AM$ and $BC$ meet at $N$. Prove that lines $CM$, $FN$, and $AE$ are concurrent.

Two players play a game starting with an empty graph on $S$ vertices and $k$ pencils of distinct colours. On each turn the first player names a colour, and the second player draws a previously undrawn edge in that colour. If a monochromatic cycle appears, the game ends and the second player wins. If all edges have been drawn without a monochromatic cycle appearing, the first player wins. For a fixed integer $S>2$, determine the largest positive integer $k$ for which the second player can guarantee a win.

Two cells of an $n\times n$ board are adjacent if they share a side. A set of cells is connected if any two cells of the set can be joined by a sequence of cells in the set in which consecutive cells are adjacent. Does there exist a positive integer $n$ for which the board can be coloured with three colours, all of which occur, so that no two adjacent cells have the same colour and, for each pair of colours, the set of cells of those two colours is connected?

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer and $a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_n,b_n$ positive real numbers such that $$\frac{a_k^2+1}{b_k}\ge b_1+\cdots+b_n,\qquad\frac{b_k^2+1}{a_k}\ge a_1+\cdots+a_n$$ for every $k=1,\ldots,n$. Prove that $$|a_1-b_1|+\cdots+|a_n-b_n|\le\sqrt{8n}.$$

The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ meet at $E$. Let $I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4$ be the incenters of $ABE$, $BCE$, $CDE$, $DAE$, respectively, and let $\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3,\omega_4$ be the circumcircles of $ABI_1$, $BCI_2$, $CDI_3$, $DAI_4$, respectively. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AC$ and $BD$. Prove that, if $M\ne N$, there is a point $P$ on line $MN$ with equal powers with respect to all four circles. The power of a point $X$ with respect to a circle with centre $O$ and radius $r$ is $OX^2-r^2$.
